name: European Commission DG Competition - merger case register (competition-cases.ec.europa.eu) + EU Official Journal C notices via EUR-Lex / Cellar
hq_country_operator: European Commission, DG Competition (Brussels); OJ publication by the Publications Office of the EU (Luxembourg)
data_types: EUMR concentration cases: case number (M.xxxxx), parties, notification date, provisional and actual decision dates, decision type (Art.6(1)(b), 6(1)(b) with commitments, 8(1)/8(2), prohibition, referral), simplified-procedure flag, NACE sector, decision texts, press releases, and Official Journal prior-notification notices (CONFIRMED). Merger statistics published as PDF, last updated 4 Aug 2026 (CONFIRMED).
coverage_geo: EU-27 + EEA-relevant transactions worldwide. Any deal, including one between two non-EU parties, is captured if it meets the EUMR turnover thresholds (Art.1: combined worldwide turnover EUR 5bn and EU-wide turnover EUR 250m for each of two parties, or the alternative Art.1(3) test). CONFIRMED that this excludes the entire mid-market and all purely national deals, which go to national competition authorities instead. Listed and private targets are both in scope, but only at large size.
history_depth: Cases from 21 September 1990 (entry into force of the original Merger Regulation) to present; database updated daily on weekdays 10:00-11:00 CET (CONFIRMED on ec.europa.eu/competition/mergers/cases/about_this_site.html).
api: partial. No documented official public REST API - I inspected the site's Angular bundles and found no published API host or endpoint, and probes of /api/* return the SPA fallback (CONFIRMED by direct HTTP testing 2026-09-04). What does work: (a) the UI has a client-side Excel export of search results (xlsx writer bundled in the JS - CONFIRMED); (b) per-case and per-policy-area email notification subscriptions (CONFIRMED in bundle); (c) the machine-readable route - EUMR prior-notification notices and decisions are published in the OJ C series and ARE retrievable from the EU Publications Office Cellar SPARQL endpoint with no authentication. A live query against https://publications.europa.eu/webapi/rdf/sparql returned titles such as Prior notification of a concentration (Case M.8283 - General Electric Company/LM Wind Power Holding) (CONFIRMED, tested 2026-09-04).
bulk_delivery: No official bulk dump of the case register. Workable substitutes: XLSX export of search results from the UI; SPARQL/REST harvesting of OJ C notices from Cellar; per-case document downloads. Third-party scrapers exist (e.g. an Apify EC merger/antitrust scraper) but are unofficial and outside Commission terms (INFERRED).
pricing: Free (CONFIRMED - public Commission website, no account or fee).
ml_training_license: CONFIRMED permissive. The Commission legal notice cites Commission Decision 2011/833/EU on the reuse of Commission documents and licenses EU-owned content under CC BY 4.0 - reuse allowed, including commercially, with attribution and indication of changes. Excludes logos, trade marks and third-party rights. CC BY 4.0 imposes no restriction on model training (INFERRED from the licence text). Materially better than any commercial provider.
language: Case metadata and Phase I notices in all EU official languages; Phase I full decision texts in the original language only; Phase II full texts in EN/FR/DE with summaries in all EU languages (CONFIRMED). No Japanese.
fit_for_lead_prediction: High-precision, low-recall. Excellent as a gold-standard labelled set of large announced/completed deals with clean party names, dates and sector codes - useful for training and for validating other sources. Useless as a mid-market lead source: EUMR thresholds mean roughly 300-400 notifications a year, essentially all large-cap. For a Japanese mid-market advisory this is a reference spine, not a pipeline. Pre-notification contacts are never disclosed, so there is no early-warning signal (CONFIRMED).
budget_tier: free - Free, no registration, no paid tier. [Europe option #1, researched 2026-09-04]

name: National Officially Appointed Mechanisms (OAMs) under Transparency Directive 2004/109/EC - FCA NSM (UK), info-financiere.gouv.fr (France), AFM (NL), Unternehmensregister (DE), 1Info / eMarket STORAGE (IT), CNMV (ES), SIX Exchange Regulation (CH), Oslo Bors NewsWeb (NO)
hq_country_operator: ~30 separate national operators - securities regulators (FCA, AMF/AIFE, AFM, CONSOB, CNMV), company registers (Germany), or licensed private mechanisms (Computershare 1Info, Teleborsa eMarket STORAGE, SIX Exchange Regulation)
data_types: Regulated information for listed issuers: annual and half-year financial reports, major-shareholding / threshold-crossing notifications (the single best public signal of stake-building and creeping control), inside information and ad-hoc releases under MAR, takeover offer documents and offeror statements, director dealings, total voting rights (CONFIRMED across the OAMs checked).
coverage_geo: EU-27 plus Norway/Iceland/Liechtenstein via the EEA, plus the UK (FCA NSM, post-Brexit onshored DTRs) and Switzerland (SIX Exchange Regulation, non-EEA but an equivalent regime). Listed companies only - no private-company deal coverage at all (CONFIRMED).
history_depth: Varies widely. France: filings retrievable back to at least 2012 with direct PDF links, AMF BDIF decisions from 1997. UK NSM: Morningstar-operated from 2009, FCA-operated from 2020 (INFERRED). Switzerland SIX significant shareholdings: back to 1 January 1998 (CONFIRMED). Netherlands AFM: historic notifications from 1991/1996 as PDF (CONFIRMED). Italy: 1Info authorised 2014, eMarket STORAGE 2022 (CONFIRMED).
api: partial, country by country. FRANCE is best in class: info-financiere.gouv.fr exposes a free Opendatasoft Explore v2.0/v2.1 REST API with NO API key, ~10,000 calls/IP/day, Swagger docs, and records carrying issuer name, ISIN, information type, filing date and a direct PDF URL (CONFIRMED - live calls made). NETHERLANDS: the AFM substantial-holdings register offers free CSV and XML export with no login, plus a daily email change service (CONFIRMED), but no REST API. UK: FCA NSM is free with CSV export of search results but has NO public retrieval API, and FCA material indicates programmatic access is not permitted (CONFIRMED free/CSV; INFERRED on the prohibition). GERMANY, ITALY, SPAIN, NORWAY: free web viewing only, no free official API; Spain's machine-readable hechos relevantes feed is a paid BME SFTP product (CONFIRMED). Switzerland SIX: free searchable database, no export or API documented.
bulk_delivery: France: Opendatasoft /exports/ endpoints (CSV/JSON/Parquet). Netherlands: CSV/XML register export. UK: legacy ZIP of 2009-2020 URL mappings only. Elsewhere none official. Unofficial German full-register dumps exist via OffeneRegister.de (INFERRED).
pricing: Free to search and download documents in every OAM checked (CONFIRMED). Paid only where a machine-readable feed is resold by an exchange or data vendor; those prices are not published.
ml_training_license: Mixed. France is explicitly Etalab Open Licence 2.0 - free reuse including commercial and derivative works (CONFIRMED); Etalab 2.0 is CC-BY-compatible and does not bar model training (INFERRED). Other OAMs publish no reuse licence, so status is UNCONFIRMED and defaults to national copyright plus site terms; UK NSM and Spain appear to restrict systematic extraction (INFERRED). Treat France and the Netherlands as safe and have qualified counsel review the rest before any bulk ingestion.
language: National languages, with English common for UK, Dutch and Nordic issuers. France, Germany, Italy and Spain are predominantly local-language. No Japanese.
update_frequency: Real-time to daily as issuers file (CONFIRMED). Switzerland SIX publishes the next trading day by 07:30.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The richest free signal set for European listed-company M&A - major-holdings notifications reveal stake-building weeks before an offer, and offer documents give terms. But it is ~30 separate integrations, mostly without APIs, in ~15 languages. Realistic sequencing: build France and the Netherlands first (free API and free exports), add the UK NSM by CSV, and defer the rest until ESAP absorbs them. Covers listed targets only, so it does not reach the private mid-market where JCAI mainly operates.
budget_tier: free - Free to view everywhere. Machine-readable feeds are free in France and the Netherlands; commercial in Spain (BME SFTP), the UK (LSEG RNS vendor licence) and Norway (Euronext). [Europe option #2, researched 2026-09-04]

name: Moody's Orbis M&A (formerly Zephyr, Bureau van Dijk)
hq_country_operator: Moody's Analytics / Bureau van Dijk (Brussels; Moody's Corporation, New York)
data_types: M&A, IPO, private equity and venture capital transactions - announced, pending, completed, withdrawn and rumoured. Deal value, stake percentage, financing, advisers, and integration with Orbis company financials on both sides of the deal (CONFIRMED via vendor pages and subscriber institutions).
coverage_geo: Global with a genuine European bias - Zephyr was built in Europe and Europe remains its deepest region. Critically there is NO minimum deal-size threshold, so it captures small private-company transactions that Mergermarket and LSEG omit (CONFIRMED via Aalto University and KU Leuven subscriber documentation). That is precisely the segment a Japanese mid-market advisory needs for European targets.
history_depth: European deals from 1997; US and rest of world from 2001 (CONFIRMED via Aalto University data-source page, corroborated by KU Leuven). Deal count around 1.8m-2.3m including rumours, roughly 100-150k added annually (INFERRED - figures conflict across sources and do not appear on a Moody's page).
api: partial / UNCONFIRMED for this specific product. Web platform confirmed. Moody's Data Hub advertises delivery by feeds, APIs and an MCP server and lists Mergers and acquisitions as a data type, but does not name Orbis M&A as API-delivered (CONFIRMED wording, INFERRED applicability). A third-party integration document confirms an Orbis enrichment API exists with a licensed key. Bulk or flat-file delivery of Orbis M&A: UNCONFIRMED - must be requested from Moody's and written into the contract.
bulk_delivery: UNCONFIRMED. Platform-first product; assume seat-based access unless a data-feed specification is obtained in writing.
pricing: NOT PUBLISHED by Moody's (CONFIRMED - no price on any vendor page fetched). A UK G-Cloud 14 Orbis pricing document exists on the Digital Marketplace and would be a real, contractually binding public price list worth retrieving manually (UNCONFIRMED contents - the PDF did not parse). Do not rely on the USD 20k-50k per user per year band circulating on comparison blogs; that figure originates from a competitor's marketing page and is directional only.
ml_training_license: CONFIRMED HOSTILE by default. The Moody's global copyright notice states that no information may be used to develop, improve, train or retrain any software program or database, including for artificial intelligence, machine learning or natural language processing software, and bars repackaging, redistribution and storage for subsequent use. Caveat: that is the general moodys.com notice, not a negotiated Orbis subscription agreement (the Orbis terms page returned HTTP 403). Any plan to train a lead-scoring model on this data must be negotiated explicitly into the licence and reviewed by qualified counsel before signature - a legal question, not one this research can settle.
language: English interface and deal records; company data multilingual with local-language names.
update_frequency: Daily (INFERRED from vendor positioning; exact cadence not published).
fit_for_lead_prediction: The only realistic single source of broad pan-European PRIVATE mid-market deal history, filling the gap the free official sources structurally cannot. Strong for comparables, adviser mapping and buyer-behaviour modelling on European targets. Two blockers before procurement: (1) renegotiate the ML and derivative-works prohibition in writing; (2) confirm bulk or API delivery exists, since seat-based platform access will not support internal analytics at scale. Cheaper alternatives were checked and are weaker for Europe: Mergr is USD 150/month (CONFIRMED on its pricing page) but publishes no European coverage breakdown and caps standard exports at 250 records; MergerLinks was acquired by Datasite in August 2023 and is adviser/dealmaker intelligence, not a deal database. Mergermarket, Dealroom and OpenCorporates are already on the firm's provider list.
budget_tier: enterprise - Enterprise subscription, seat-based, negotiated. No public price list. [Europe option #3, researched 2026-09-04]

name: ESMA registers and databases today (Prospectus III, FIRDS) + European Single Access Point (ESAP) from 2027 - Regulation (EU) 2023/2859
hq_country_operator: European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), Paris
data_types: TODAY: the EU-wide register of approved prospectuses (Prospectus III documents and securities, with issuer name and LEI, home and host country, security type, ISIN, CFI, offer type, consideration offered, EU Growth flag, approval and passporting dates) - relevant to M&A because share-for-share offers, listings and capital raises require a prospectus. Also FIRDS instrument reference data, benchmarks, funds, sanctions and STS notifications. FROM 2027 via ESAP: Transparency Directive filings, prospectuses and short-selling data in Phase 1; accounting, MAR, SFDR and UCITS in Phase 2; MiFID II, AIFMD, CRR and the Takeover Bids Directive in Phase 3.
coverage_geo: EU-27 / EEA, fed by national competent authorities. No UK and no Switzerland (CONFIRMED - both outside the EU regime).
history_depth: Prospectus III register is live and large - a direct query returned a very high indexed document count across issuers (CONFIRMED, tested 2026-09-04). FIRDS published-instrument file register returned 18,610 files (CONFIRMED). ESAP will hold data from its collection start rather than retrospectively (INFERRED).
api: yes, today, and better than expected. ESMA Registers exposes documented machine-to-machine (A2A) Solr services with NO authentication plus predefined full-dataset extraction queries. Live calls to https://registers.esma.europa.eu/solr/esma_registers_priii_documents/select?q=*:*&rows=1&wt=json and to the FIRDS files core both returned JSON (CONFIRMED, tested 2026-09-04). Documented cores include priii_documents, priii_securities, upreg, funds, bench_*, sanctions, stsre and mifid_shsexs. FOR ESAP: Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 requires collection bodies to feed ESAP through a single API and requires ESAP to offer API access and machine-readable data (CONFIRMED via the AMF summary); technical specifications sit in delegated acts.
bulk_delivery: Yes - the A2A help file publishes predefined full-dataset Solr extraction URLs per register with rows parameters (CONFIRMED). FIRDS full and delta files are downloadable. ESAP bulk and API specifications remain in delegated acts (UNCONFIRMED detail).
pricing: Free (CONFIRMED - open Solr endpoints with no authentication; ESAP free access mandated by regulation).
ml_training_license: UNCONFIRMED for the ESMA registers - ESMA publishes no explicit reuse licence on the A2A help page. ESAP data is public regulatory information intended for free reuse and the Regulation is built around machine readability, but exact reuse terms are not yet settled (INFERRED). Have counsel confirm before bulk ingestion.
language: English metadata; underlying prospectuses in national languages. ESAP is required to be searchable in all EU official languages (CONFIRMED).
update_frequency: ESMA registers refreshed regularly from NCA feeds (CONFIRMED - records carry timestamps). ESAP: collection from 10 July 2026, public go-live by 10 July 2027.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Today a useful secondary signal rather than a deal source - prospectus approvals flag share-for-share offers, IPOs and listing-related transactions, and the free keyless API makes it cheap to ingest. The strategic point is ESAP: from July 2027 it becomes the closest thing Europe will have to EDGAR/EDINET, free and API-first. Note the timing trap - Takeover Bids Directive disclosure is Phase 3 from 10 January 2030 (CONFIRMED via AMF), so ESAP will not be an M&A deal register for at least four more years. Build toward it, do not wait for it. Relevant precedent: ESMA's earlier European Electronic Access Point (Transparency Directive Art.21a) was suspended in 2018 and never launched, and Art.21a has since been repealed by the ESAP Omnibus Directive (EU) 2023/2864 (INFERRED-strong) - a caution against assuming EU aggregation projects land on schedule.
budget_tier: free - Free now, and free by law under ESAP - Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 requires access free of charge. [Europe option #4, researched 2026-09-04]

name: EU business register interconnection (BRIS via the European e-Justice Portal) + national company registers, incl. UK Companies House API
hq_country_operator: European Commission DG JUST (BRIS central platform); national business registers of EU-27 plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway; Companies House (UK, Cardiff)
data_types: Company name, legal form, registered office, registration number, EUID, status, and links to national register records; branch and cross-border merger and conversion notifications flow between registers. Companies House adds officers, the PSC beneficial-ownership register, filing history and accounts.
coverage_geo: EU-27 plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway through BRIS (CONFIRMED); the UK separately via Companies House; Switzerland via Zefix, not in BRIS.
history_depth: Live register state rather than history - BRIS queries national registers in real time and holds no archive of its own (CONFIRMED). Companies House holds filing history going back decades.
api: no for BRIS - there is no API, no programmatic access and no bulk data through the e-Justice portal, which makes it unusable for at-scale screening (CONFIRMED-strong; consistent across Commission and practitioner sources). Yes for Companies House - free REST API with a registered key plus bulk company data products; already on the firm's provider list, so treat as covered.
bulk_delivery: None from BRIS. Companies House publishes free monthly bulk company data and accounts data. Unofficial German register dumps exist via OffeneRegister.de (INFERRED).
pricing: BRIS search is free, and only data that is free in the underlying national register is free through the portal (CONFIRMED via Commission BRIS material). Companies House API is free with a registered key.
ml_training_license: Companies House data is under the UK Open Government Licence, permitting commercial reuse and derivative works (INFERRED - standard for Companies House products; confirm on their licence page). BRIS reuse terms UNCONFIRMED and governed by each national register.
language: Portal in all EU official languages; register records in national languages.
update_frequency: Real time (BRIS queries live); Companies House near real time with monthly bulk snapshots.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Not a deal source - this is the entity-resolution backbone. Its job is to normalise European counterparty names, resolve group structures and ownership, and provide a stable company identifier to hang deal records on, which matters when stitching together DG COMP cases, OAM filings and a paid deal database. BRIS's lack of any API means it is a manual lookup tool only; do the programmatic work through Companies House for the UK and through national registers or a commercial aggregator elsewhere. Ranked last because it is infrastructure, not signal.
budget_tier: free - BRIS search free; some national registers charge per document. Companies House API free. [Europe option #5, researched 2026-09-04]
